title: Xanthe and the Spire
premise: Jonah Quintana's bone-carved charms have kept him fed and unnoticed in Vellharbor, a city where magic is punishable by drowning, but the night the border wards collapse and every star in the sky goes dark, his charms begin whispering with voices that are not his own. Hunted by the Wardens and guided by Xanthe—a disgraced warden who once arrested her own sister for sorcery—Jonah follows the dead to the Spire at the city's drowned heart, where he learns he is the last living heir of the covenant between the living realm and the star-dead. To reforge it before the thirteenth moon-turn, Jonah must sacrifice the voice of the dead that defines him, while Xanthe must choose between the order she swore loyalty to and the truth that her superiors broke the covenant first. In the end, Jonah gives up hearing the dead but gains something quieter: Xanthe and their found family of outcasts rebuild Vellharbor under returning stars, and the covenant is remade not by blood, but by choice.
about_author: August Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime folklore along the northern coast before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about quiet people in loud catastrophes, and insist all their books are true if you squint.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Jonah Quintana carves a charm for a dying dockworker and hears, for the first time in five years, a voice that isn't human. That same night, the border wards shatter and the stars vanish from the sky. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in wonder—the invisible life he built begins cracking open.

chapters.title: Charms for the Drowned
chapters.summary: Vellharbor panics; the Wardens sweep the markets for magic-workers. Jonah's charms start singing with the voices of the drowned dead, drawing attention he can't afford. A Warden raid forces him to flee with nothing but his carving knife. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: terror and grief as his careful anonymity dies violently.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Let Go
chapters.summary: Xanthe Corvane, a disgraced warden haunted by arresting her own sister, catches Jonah—and lets him go, because his charms hummed with her sister's voice. She becomes his reluctant ally, trading protection for answers. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: guilt meeting hope; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: A Family of Strays
chapters.summary: They shelter in the Undertow, a smuggler warren beneath the harbor run by Maren, a one-handed tide-witch, and Pip, a feral child who can walk through wards. The found family forms around a shared meal and shared secrets. POV: alternating Jonah and Xanthe. Emotional beat: warmth blooming in hiding—belonging neither expected.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: The drowned dead guide Jonah toward the Spire at the harbor's heart, revealing fragments: the covenant between realms was broken deliberately, thirteen turns ago, by the Wardens' founders. Xanthe realizes her order's holiest law is a lie. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: loyalty fracturing against truth.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: The moon enters its final cycle; without the covenant, the star-dead will pour through the fallen wards. The Wardens declare martial law and begin public drownings of suspected magic-users—including someone from the Undertow. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: rage and resolve; hiding is no longer possible or acceptable.

chapters.title: Sister of Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Xanthe confronts High Warden Aldous Vey, who reveals her sister wasn't executed but bound into the Spire as its failing anchor. He offers Xanthe absolution if she delivers Jonah. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: betrayal weaponized—her deepest wound used as a leash.

chapters.title: The Drowned Road
chapters.summary: Guided by Pip's ward-walking and Maren's tide-craft, the group crosses the flooded old city to reach the Spire, losing supplies and nearly each other. Jonah confesses what reforging the covenant will cost him: the voice of the dead. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: love against duty—he chooses the world over himself, quietly.

chapters.title: The Spire at the Heart of the Harbor
chapters.summary: Climax. Inside the Spire, Xanthe finds her sister half-dissolved into the anchor-stone; Vey arrives with Wardens to kill Jonah and preserve the lie. Xanthe breaks her oath publicly, fights Vey, and frees her sister's spirit while Jonah begins the reforging as the thirteenth turn completes. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: everything breaking so it can be remade.

chapters.title: A Quieter Voice
chapters.summary: Jonah completes the covenant, sacrificing his gift—the dead fall silent, and the stars return one by one over Vellharbor. Vey falls; the Wardens reform under new oaths. Months later, Jonah carves ordinary charms, no longer hearing whispers, surrounded by chosen family. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—what was lost made room for what was found.
